title: Exactness for the normalized shift comparison on the recorded intrinsic rational stages.
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and finite intermediate coefficient fields $E\subseteq L\subseteq\Omega$ [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Let $Y$ be any scheme. Write $\mathcal I_F=D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_F)$ for the intrinsic derived-complete integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], with its inherited triangulation [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated], and $\mathcal R_F=\mathcal I_F[1/\varpi_F]$, with localization $Q_F:\mathcal I_F\to\mathcal R_F$, for its raw rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated], for $F=E,L$. Let $T:\mathcal I_E\to\mathcal I_L$ be completed integral scalar extension restricted to these categories [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension, lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible]. Let $G:D(Y,\mathcal O_E)\to D(Y,\mathcal O_L)$ be ordinary derived extension of the completed coefficient sheaves, and put $H=G\circ I_E$, where $I_E:\mathcal I_E\hookrightarrow D(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ and $I_L:\mathcal I_L\hookrightarrow D(Y,\mathcal O_L)$ are the inclusions. Give $H$ its specified ordinary derived coherent integer-shift comparison $h_{n,K}:H(K[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}H(K)[n]$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization, lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Let $\chi:H\xrightarrow{\sim}I_L\circ T$ be the fixed ordinary-to-completed natural isomorphism [def-zl-normalized-integral-scalar-comparison], and write $\beta_{n,Z}:I_L(Z[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}I_L(Z)[n]$ for the inherited inclusion comparison. Suppose $t$ is a coherent integer-shift comparison on $T$, meaning natural isomorphisms $t_{n,K}:T(K[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}(TK)[n]$ satisfying the zero and addition equations, and suppose its normalization is, for every $n,K$,
$$
I_L(t_{n,K});\beta_{n,TK}=\chi_{K[n]}^{-1};h_{n,K};\chi_K[n].
$$
Let $F:\mathcal R_E\longrightarrow\mathcal R_L$ be the specified scalar transition [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], with $F(Q_EK)=Q_L(TK)$ and $F(f\otimes a)=T(f)\otimes\iota(a)$. Suppose $c$ is a coherent integer-shift comparison on $F$, meaning natural isomorphisms $c_n:F(-[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}(F-)[n]$ satisfying the zero and addition equations, and suppose its degree-one component satisfies
$$
 c_{1,Q_EK}=Q_L(t_{1,K})\qquad(K\in\mathcal I_E).
$$
Then $F$ with this prescribed comparison is exact [def-weil-triangulated-category]: for every distinguished triangle
$$X\xrightarrow{u}Y'\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{w}X[1]$$
of $\mathcal R_E$, the triangle
$$FX\xrightarrow{F(u)}FY'\xrightarrow{F(v)}FZ\xrightarrow{\ c_{1,X}\circ F(w)\ }(FX)[1]$$
is distinguished in $\mathcal R_L$. Thus the assertion concerns every coherent pair $(t,c)$ satisfying the displayed normalization equations, and in particular the recorded normalized transition. No structure morphism from $Y$ to a finite field is assumed.

proof.text: Let $I_E,I_L$ be the integral full-subcategory inclusions and let $G$ be ordinary derived extension along the map $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\to S=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}$ of completed coefficient sheaves. By [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], $S$ is a finite free $R$-module sheaf; after choosing a basis, termwise change of rings $-\otimes_RS$ is, on underlying sheaves, a finite direct sum of copies of the identity, hence an exact functor of module sheaves. So [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], clause (1), makes $G$ with its termwise shift comparison an exact functor; this is the derived-tensor shift entering $h$. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], clause (2), $G$ is the derived change of rings $-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RS$: for a K-flat resolution $P\to K$, the termwise exact functor carries it to a quasi-isomorphism $P\otimes_RS\to K\otimes_RS$. [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated] makes $I_E$ exact, so $H=G\circ I_E$ with the composite comparison $h$ is exact. The finite-free completion comparison is an isomorphism, natural on all derived-complete objects, by [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Use its fixed quotient-completion normalization $\chi:H\xrightarrow{\sim}I_L\circ T$ from [def-zl-normalized-integral-scalar-comparison]. The restriction $T$ lands in $\mathcal I_L$ by [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible]. These results apply for arbitrary $Y$; finiteness is required only of the coefficient fields.

proof.text:
For a distinguished integral triangle $\Delta=(A\to B\to C\xrightarrow{\delta}A[1])$, write $h$ for the shift of $H$ and $\beta$ for that of $I_L$. The displayed normalization hypothesis in the statement says $I_L(t_{1,A});\beta_A=\chi_{A[1]}^{-1};h_A;\chi_A[1]$, where semicolons mean composition in order. Consequently naturality of $\chi$ gives
$$\chi_C;I_L(T\delta);I_L(t_{1,A});\beta_A=H\delta;h_A;\chi_A[1].$$
Together with naturality on the first two arrows, this makes the three components of $\chi$ an isomorphism from the distinguished triangle $H\Delta$ to the included triangle $T\Delta$ with connecting arrow $T\delta;t_{1,A}$. The latter is distinguished by invariance under isomorphism [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Distinguished triangles in $\mathcal I_L$ are exactly the ambient distinguished triangles lying in it [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated]; hence $T\Delta$ is distinguished for the prescribed $t$.

proof.text:
For an integral morphism $a$, the pure-tensor formula in [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] gives $F(Q_Ea)=Q_L(Ta)$, since $Q_Ea=a\otimes1$. The displayed relation $Q_F\circ[1]=[1]\circ Q_F$ makes the degree-one comparison of each $Q_F$ the identity, and the displayed degree-one normalization hypothesis gives $c_{1,Q_EA}=Q_L(t_{1,A})$. Thus the first two arrows of $F(Q_E\Delta)$ are $Q_L(Ta)$, and its last arrow is exactly
$$F(Q_E\delta);c_{1,Q_EA}=Q_L(T\delta);Q_L(t_{1,A})=Q_L(T\delta;t_{1,A}).$$
All object and degree-one shift identifications here are the fixed ones in that normalization. Hence this entire triangle is $Q_L(T\Delta)$, which is distinguished by step 2 and exactness of $Q_L$ [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated]. The Lean proof invokes the proved rational-transition-from-integral lemma, with the normalized integral shift and its exactness established in the preceding step; its hypothesis is exactly transitionCommShift_existsUnique at degree one.

source.place: Tag 05R6, proposition-construct-localization; direct evaluation of the pure-tensor and normalized degree-one formulas

proof.text: Every distinguished triangle $\Gamma$ in $\mathcal R_E$ is isomorphic to $Q_E\Delta$ for an integral distinguished triangle $\Delta$, by [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated]. Apply $F$ to the three components of this isomorphism. Naturality of $c_1$ supplies its last triangle square, so these components give an isomorphism of mapped triangles; applying $F$ to the inverse gives its inverse. Step 3 and invariance of distinguished triangles under isomorphism show that $F\Gamma$ is distinguished. This is precisely exactness for the given shift comparison [def-weil-triangulated-category].
